clue.text: The first male worker in firm

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man created
the ant is the crossword's standard worker, from the worker caste of the colony

explanation.surface: A company's original male employee, the founding hand in the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like the business the worker is in, but it is the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone firm in a position is unyielding and immovable.

clue.text: Sharp detectives in US intelligence set-up

indicators.note: the detectives' letters are placed in the middle of the other piece
in a down clue, 'set up' means the letters are raised, so read bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the United States
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Pointed remark about British detectives working inside an American spy operation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set-up' means raised, so the agency's letters read upwards; 'Sharp' is a taste, not cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sharp taste is sour or acidic, like vinegar or lemon.

clue.text: A ruined lodge that's been around for centuries

indicators.note: a ruined building has fallen apart, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A tumbledown hunting lodge that has stood for hundreds of years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges A LODGE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: something ancient has existed for ages, over many generations.

clue.text: Support for Nigella, ace when cooking

indicators.note: cooking ingredients changes them, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Fans backing Nigella Lawson, the TV cook, who is brilliant in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooking' rearranges NIGELLA ACE. Nigella Lawson is a well-known British television cook, which makes the cooking surface natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: loyal support for a cause or ruler is fidelity to it.

clue.text: Rents and rates revised

indicators.note: something revised is reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord's notice: rents and rates have been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rents' is not money paid but the plural of a rip, and 'revised' rearranges RATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rents are rips in cloth, and so are tears.

clue.text: These describe Met lines, as Boris found out

indicators.note: 'out' signals letters put out of their order, so the fodder is scrambled

explanation.surface: A politician named Boris learns about lines on a weather chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' rearranges AS BORIS. The Met is the Met Office, Britain's weather service, whose charts are drawn with these lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: on weather maps, curves join places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Breaks in and bangs on the head

parts.note: bangs, in American usage, are hair cut short across the forehead, called fringes in Britain

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in and hits someone over the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bangs on the head' suggests blows, but it is hair over the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to break a rule or law is to violate or transgress it.

clue.text: Arab state offering appeal to the masculine type

parts.note: O is the vocative cry used when calling on or appealing to someone
a male person, a man

explanation.surface: A Gulf country putting out an advert pitched at macho men.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sultanate on the south-east coast of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Illumination provided by a half-moon?

parts.note: a half-moon is a curved bow shape, so its glow is a lamp named after that curve, the bright lamp of film sets

explanation.surface: Light shed by the moon at its quarter phase.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-moon is a curved segment, and the clue reads that curve plus the glow as the name of an intense electric lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an intense lamp whose glow comes from a spark leaping across a gap between electrodes.

clue.text: Fellow travellers may opt for these cocktails

definitions.text: Fellow travellers may opt for these
definitions.meaning: attachments to a motorcycle in which a passenger travels alongside the rider
a brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice drink

explanation.surface: Companions on a trip might choose these mixed drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow travellers' usually means political sympathisers, but here it is literal: passengers riding beside a motorcyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: one a passenger pod bolted to a motorbike, the other a classic brandy-based drink.

clue.text: Perfect one piece of business

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A flawless single business transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something perfect is the best imaginable, flawless.

clue.text: Promised to go into a union

definitions.text: Promised to go into a union

parts.words: Promised to go into a union
parts.note: a person promised in marriage is engaged, the union being a wedding rather than a trade union

explanation.surface: A worker pledged to join a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a labour organisation; the union meant is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone betrothed or engaged has promised to marry.

clue.text: Groundless rumour of busybody on the dole?

parts.note: someone on the dole, receiving unemployment benefit, is out of work
a busybody who spreads tales is a gossip

explanation.surface: Baseless tittle-tattle spread by a nosy unemployed person.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the everyday British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: chatter with no basis in fact, trivial talk spread for amusement.

clue.text: Girl starts to suspect criminal record

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the starts of the words that follow are their first letters

explanation.surface: A young woman begins to suspect someone has a criminal history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal record' reads as one phrase, but 'record' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vinyl record is a flat round disc of music.

clue.text: I agree cost is incorporated in order

indicators.note: letters incorporated are worked together into a new body, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: Accepting that a cost is built into an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is incorporated' rearranges I AGREE COST.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to order things is to sort them into classes or groups.

clue.text: He's a fine script writer

parts.note: the phrase suggests a talented screenwriter, but script here is handwriting, and fine means elegant

explanation.surface: Praise for a talented screenwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'script writer' suggests films; the script is penmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an artist of decorative handwriting who forms fine lettering with a pen.

clue.text: Really fired up congregation about end of service

parts.note: something fired up has been lit

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering of people

explanation.surface: An excited church congregation goes into raptures at the close of a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the rally around, i.e. after, the last letter of 'service'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: used as an intensifier, both words mean actually or truly.

clue.text: A literary supplement?

parts.note: the phrase suggests a review section of a newspaper, but means an addition at the end of a book

explanation.surface: A newspaper's books section, such as a weekly review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literary supplement' evokes a review magazine; here it is simply extra material added to a written work.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an appendix of extra material printed at the end of a book.

clue.text: Had a second look at something?

definitions.text: Had a second look at something?

parts.words: Had a second look at something?
parts.note: a second look suggests a repeat inspection, but a second here is a moment, so the look was fleeting

explanation.surface: Checked something again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second look' wants to mean looking again; read 'second' as a brief instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: caught a brief, momentary sight of something in passing.

clue.text: Licensed eats may be ordered here

definitions.text: Licensed eats may be ordered here

indicators.note: letters that are ordered are arranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: You can order permitted food at this shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be ordered' rearranges LICENSED EATS, and the whole clue describes the shop too.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods, where such fare is bought.

clue.text: Saved, but still confined to bed

definitions.meaning: stored away for future use, put by

explanation.surface: A patient rescued from danger yet still bedridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saved' suggests rescued, but it means stored away, as supplies are.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic senses of the same phrasal verb: stored for later, and kept in bed by illness.

clue.text: Delight in exercising round the fields

indicators.note: the exercise letters go round the fields, enclosing them

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word

explanation.surface: Joy found in a workout around the meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to delight someone is to gratify or satisfy them.

clue.text: Some of them maybe will feature in Austen novel

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Perhaps a few of these characters will appear in a Jane Austen book.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'will feature in Austen novel' as the definition; 'will feature in' is only a link, so the definition is 'Austen novel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jane Austen's 1815 novel about a matchmaking heroine in Highbury.

clue.text: A fight, but nobody is charged

definitions.meaning: a brawl in which everyone joins in
at no cost to anyone, gratis to every person

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out, but the police press no charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests accused by police; the second sense is about paying nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a chaotic brawl open to anyone, and something given at no cost to everyone.

clue.text: Noblemen going to court in London?

definitions.text: Noblemen going to court in London?

parts.words: Noblemen going to court in London?
parts.note: peers attending court suggests royalty, but adding court to their title gives a district of west London

explanation.surface: Aristocrats heading to a royal court in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Earls Court is a district of west London, known for its exhibition centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: peers of the rank above viscount and below marquess.

clue.text: Going off in great spirits

definitions.meaning: meat or game starting to rot and smell strongly

explanation.surface: Someone leaving in a jolly mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' suggests leaving; here it means food turning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: game hung until gamey and smelling, and elated or euphoric.

clue.text: To succeed in business one must keep still

definitions.text: To succeed in business one must keep still

parts.words: To succeed in business one must keep still
parts.note: advice to stay calm, but a still is the apparatus for making spirits, which this trader must keep

explanation.surface: Business advice: stay calm and motionless to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep still' reads as stay motionless; it means own and run a still, the apparatus for making whisky or gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a maker of spirits such as whisky, who runs stills.

clue.text: Country needs aid in getting into shape

indicators.note: the letters are moulded into a new form, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation needs help to get fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into shape' rearranges AID IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a nation of South Asia, the world's most populous.

clue.text: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?

definitions.text: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?

parts.words: Openly took advantage of the sunshine?
parts.note: from the proverb about seizing a chance while the sun shines, here read literally of farmers drying grass in the open

explanation.surface: Publicly made the most of the fine weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says make it while the sun shines; 'Openly' hints at the open fields where cut grass is dried.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: seized an opportunity, literally dried cut grass for fodder in good weather.

clue.text: Jack will work on this ecclesiastical point

definitions.text: Jack will work on this ecclesiastical point

parts.words: Jack will work on this ecclesiastical point
parts.note: Jack looks like a man's name, but joined to the answer it names a worker who repairs tall towers

explanation.surface: A man called Jack will make a point about church matters.
explanation.walkthrough: A steeplejack climbs and repairs church spires and chimneys.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a church's pointed tower, topped by a spire.
